Operating Characteristics of the BOIN-ETC Design

Source: R/sim_boin_etc.R
sim_boin_etc.Rd

Simulate trials of the BOIN-ETC design of Kakizume et al. (2024) for two drugs given together with boin_etc_simulate, select the optimal dose combination (ODC) of every trial with boin_etc_select_obd, and summarize the selection percentages and the numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at every combination.

Usage

sim_boin_etc(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  subtrials = c("etc1", "etc2", "etc3"),
  n_earlystop = 6,
  etc1_start = c("diagonal", "below"),
  rule4 = c("paper", "authors_code"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6),
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  p_eli = NULL,
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  odc_tie = c("lowest", "all"),
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, phi.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, delta, as in sim_boin_et.

p_true

Numeric matrix. True DLT probability of every combination, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B. At least two levels of each drug.

p_resp

Numeric matrix of the same size. True response probability of every combination.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial; with cohort_size it gives the maximum sample size.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

subtrials

Character scalar. The division of the dose matrix into subtrials and their starting combinations: "etc1" (the default), "etc2" or "etc3", BOIN-ETC1, 2 and 3 of the figures and tables of Kakizume et al. (2024). See Details.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. A subtrial ends when the combination chosen for the next cohort has this many patients (n_stop of Kakizume et al., 2024). Defaults to 6.

etc1_start

Character scalar. Starting combination of a row subtrial of "etc1": "diagonal" (the default) one level of drug B below the candidate of the previous subtrial, as the text and the figures of Kakizume et al. (2024) state; "below" the same level of drug B, the rule of the code of the authors that produced their published results. See Details.

rule4

Character scalar. Choice among the neighboring combinations when the DLT rate is between lambda1 and lambda2 and the response rate at most eta1: "paper" (the default) the rule of the text; "authors_code" the rule of the code of the authors, needed to reproduce their results for BOIN-ETC1. See Details.

p_saf, p_tox, p_saf_resp, prior

Design parameters of the BOIN-ET boundaries, as in boin_et_boundary. The defaults give (lambda1, lambda2, eta1) = (0.14, 0.35, 0.48) for a target DLT probability of 0.30 and a target response probability of 0.60.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A combination is excluded, with the higher combinations of its subtrial, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds p_eli is above this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the exclusion rule. Defaults to NULL, target.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type. Defaults to 0, as in the simulations of Kakizume et al. (2024); the BOIN-ET functions default to 0.2.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) or "binary", as in sim_boin_et.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utilities of a patient with neither a DLT nor a response and with both; a response without DLT scores 100 and a DLT without response 0. Default to 40 and 60, the utilities (100, 40, 60, 0) of Kakizume et al. (2024).

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a combination divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

odc_tie

Character scalar. "lowest" (the default) counts one ODC per trial, the tied candidate with the lowest sum of the levels; "all" counts every tied candidate as selected, the definition of the published percentages of Kakizume et al. (2024), so that sel_percent can add up to more than 100.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the simulated trials (trials) and the selection (obd, tied) in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Print progress messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin_etc_oc, which is a list with components

design

"BOIN-ETC1", "BOIN-ETC2" or "BOIN-ETC3".

target, target_resp, p_true, p_resp

The targets and the true probabilities.

n_rows, n_cols, n_trials

Numbers of levels of drug A and drug B, and of trials.

lambda1, lambda2, eta1

The BOIN-ET boundaries.

sel_percent

Matrix of the percentage of trials selecting each combination as the ODC.

percent_no_obd, percent_early_stop

Percentages of trials selecting no ODC and stopped early.

n_pts_dose, n_tox_dose, n_resp_dose

Matrices of the average numbers of patients, DLTs and responses at each combination.

total_n_pts, total_n_tox, total_n_resp

Their totals.

mean_subtrials

Average number of subtrials run.

true_obd

Two-column matrix of the true optimal combinations: the combinations with the highest true utility among those with a DLT probability at most target.

pct_true_obd_selected, pct_patients_true_obd

Percentage of trials selecting a true optimal combination (with odc_tie = "all", the sum of sel_percent over them) and percentage of the patients treated there.

overdose

List with the cutoff (target), the combinations above it, and the percentages of trials selecting one of them (pct_selected) and of patients treated there (pct_patients).

stop_reason_percent

Percentage of trials by stopping reason.

odc_tie, settings, call

The settings used.

trials, obd, tied

With keep_trials = TRUE, the boin_etc_trials object, a two-column matrix of the selected combinations and the logical array of the tied candidates.

Details

The percentages of patients are those of the average numbers of patients. Kakizume et al. (2024) report the average over trials of the percentage of the patients of a trial treated at the optimal combinations ( from trials, as in inst/reproduce/reproduce_Kakizume2024.R. Their optimal combinations (bold in their Table 2) are not always those with the highest true utility; oc_compare accepts them through its argument truth.

References

Kakizume, T., Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2024). BOIN-ETC: A Bayesian optimal interval design considering efficacy and toxicity to identify the optimal dose combinations. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 33(4), 716-727. doi:10.1177/09622802241236936

See also

sim_boin_etc_multi, boin_etc_simulate, boin_etc_select_obd, print.boin_etc_oc

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Kakizume et al. (2024), BOIN-ETC1 with n_stop = 6
p_true <- matrix(c(0.05, 0.10, 0.10, 0.30, 0.30, 0.50), nrow = 2)
p_resp <- matrix(c(0.10, 0.25, 0.25, 0.60, 0.60, 0.65), nrow = 2)
oc <- sim_boin_etc(
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60, p_true = p_true, p_resp = p_resp,
  n_cohort = 8, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
oc
#> BOIN-ETC1 operating characteristics

#>   dose levels          : 2 of drug A, 3 of drug B

#>   utility scores       : 100, 40, 60, 0; ties lowest
#> 
#>                    Item Drug A   B1   B2   B3

#>  True response rate (%)     A1 10.0 25.0 60.0
#>                             A2 25.0 60.0 65.0
#>        OBD selected (%)     A1  1.5 14.0 31.0

#>
